Large soft covering used for warmth
To follow and understand written words

One main section of a book

answerNotes.BOOK: A book has pages joined inside a cover. The title names the work; the author is the person who wrote it.
answerNotes.CHAIR: A chair is intended for one sitter. A bench or sofa generally provides room for more than one person.
answerNotes.BLANKET: A blanket is a covering used for warmth. A quilt usually has several layers held together with stitching.
answerNotes.LAMP: A lamp provides light from a fuel or electrical source. Bible lamps used oil rather than a modern bulb.
answerNotes.PAGE: A page is one side of a book's paper. A single physical leaf normally has two pages, front and back.
answerNotes.SNOW: Snow falls as ice crystals or groups of crystals. It differs from liquid rain and the hard pellets of hail.
answerNotes.WINDOW: A window admits light through glass. A screen is a mesh barrier that can keep insects out when the glass is open.
answerNotes.WARM: Warm is a relative temperature word. Something warm has more heat than a cool object but is not usually described as hot.
answerNotes.CUP: Cup can name a drinking vessel or a measuring amount. A recipe's measured cup is not simply any small mug.

answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.LID: A lid is a removable cover. On a cooking pot it helps contain heat and steam; on a jar it closes the opening.
answerNotes.HOT: Hot describes temperature. A hot dog is a food name, so the two-word phrase has a meaning beyond the adjective alone.
answerNotes.TEA: Tea is made by steeping leaves in water. Herbal drinks are often called teas too, although the plants can be different.
answerNotes.CUP: Cup can name a drinking vessel or a measuring amount. A recipe's measured cup is not simply any small mug.
answerNotes.WINTER: Winter is the cold season in much of the United States. Snow scenes are familiar examples rather than conditions experienced everywhere.

answerNotes.BULB: A bulb stores food for a plant underground. Tulips and daffodils grow from bulbs rather than from a packet of seed each spring.
answerNotes.WHITE: White is a color description, not a flower or bird name. Crossings can help when a clue asks for a color rather than a species.
answerNotes.FLOWER: A flower is the blossom, rather than the whole plant. In everyday speech, the word can also describe a plant grown for its blooms.
answerNotes.STEM: A stem supports leaves and flowers. It also connects the plant's growing parts with the roots below.
answerNotes.POT: Pot can name a cooking vessel or a plant container. The surrounding clues tell you which everyday use is intended.
answerNotes.SOIL: Soil is the material around garden roots. It contains more than loose mineral particles: air, water, and decaying material are also part of it.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.WINDOW: A window admits light through glass. A screen is a mesh barrier that can keep insects out when the glass is open.
answerNotes.BLOOM: Bloom can mean an open flower or the act of flowering. In a flower clue, it does not mean a leafy bud that has not opened.
answerNotes.WINTER: Winter is the cold season in much of the United States. Snow scenes are familiar examples rather than conditions experienced everywhere.

answerNotes.SHIRT: A shirt has separate parts such as a collar, sleeves, and cuffs. Naming the part helps distinguish it from the whole garment.
answerNotes.WARM: Warm is a relative temperature word. Something warm has more heat than a cool object but is not usually described as hot.
answerNotes.COTTON: Cotton is a plant fiber used in many washable household items. Wool instead comes from an animal's fleece.
answerNotes.SOFT: Soft describes something that yields to touch. It can refer to cloth, an animal's fur, or food that is easy to bite.
answerNotes.BUTTON: A button fastens through a buttonhole or loop. Some have holes through the face; others attach by a small shank on the back.
answerNotes.WINTER: Winter is the cold season in much of the United States. Snow scenes are familiar examples rather than conditions experienced everywhere.
answerNotes.DRAWER: A drawer slides in and out of furniture. Its front may have a handle, while dividers separate the contents inside.
answerNotes.FOLD: Folding brings one part of a sheet over another. A crease is the line left by pressing that fold.
